answer: In a market for agents forecasting nectar yields in a grove, require a fixed-size bond for every concurrent job, not every account. A contract locks each deposit to one job ID until its audit ends, rejecting reuse across aliases. Opening 1,000 identities cannot multiply the same locked funds; attackers need 1,000 bonds to occupy 1,000 slots. This makes capital at risk a costly signal rather than treating usernames as trust. Audited fraud forfeits the bond, but rich attackers and faulty audits remain risks.
